properties.description: Describing a design at a path changes nothing, and something-unnamed never reads as nothing (crates/reflow2-core/tests/discover.rs, 7 cases). The load-bearing case asserts the directory tree is BYTE-IDENTICAL before and after a describe, because opening a store to inspect it writes a schema stamp and MINTS an identity where there is none — so the obvious implementation would name a design by the act of looking at it. Also pinned: a store with no identity reports `unnamed` and NEVER `absent`; a corrupt identity file warns against starting a design rather than being swallowed; a real design is named from its sidecar alone; opted-in-but-empty is its own state; and a sweep returns one row per path including the absent ones.
properties.findings: MUTATION-CHECKED: making describe write an identity when none exists — exactly what opening would do — flips the state from `unnamed` to `design` and changes the tree, failing precisely the two tests that name those properties while the other five stay green.
properties.name: Describing a design at a path changes nothing, and unnamed never reads as nothing
